attempts.summary: Published node4's HTTP service (port 8080) on node2's transit address port 80, and gave node1 a route to it. Built a dedicated transit link (node1 eth1 10.50.12.2/24 <-> node2 vtnet1/OPT1 10.50.12.1/24) and a dedicated lan-b link (node2 vtnet2/OPT2 10.50.24.1/24 <-> node4 enp8s0 10.50.24.2/24), assigned OPT1/OPT2 in OPNsense, added firewall pass rules, added port-forward (DNAT) rules on both the transit (OPT1) and LAN (vtnet0, serving node3's lan-a) interfaces to node4:8080, and added a hairpin source-NAT rule so lan-a-originated traffic returns correctly through node2 despite node4 also sitting on the shared default network. Bound node4's demo HTTP service only to its lan-b address so it cannot be reached by addressing node4 directly. Verified node1 and node3 both reach the service via node2:80, while direct node4:8080 access from node3 fails. All config was persisted (VyOS config.boot save, OPNsense config.xml, NetworkManager profile, systemd service, firewalld permanent rule). Completed the mandatory restart protocol on all four nodes one at a time, confirming boot-identity changes via boot_id/kern.boottime and re-verifying service health, config persistence, and end-to-end reachability after each restart.
